A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PartSAM work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original interactive and automatic segmentation experiments, architecture and training-data ablations, mesh-connectivity tests and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds benchmark results, scaling experiments, initialization and prompt-density analyses, correspondence examples and failure cases.

M1.justification: Equation (3) revises the stated objective by explicitly including IoU-MSE supervision and weighting Dice loss by alpha, specified as 2 in A.1.4, instead of the unweighted Dice term in v1. The architecture and segmentation pipeline remain substantially unchanged. Since v1 already describes training the IoU head, its explicit supervision is partly clarification; the PDFs do not establish whether the loss revision reflects retraining or corrected documentation.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained PartObjaverse-Tiny, PartNet-E and generated-shape evaluations, v3 adds coarse and fine-grained semantic-label evaluation on five 3DCoMPAT++ categories (A.3, Table 6), qualitative real-world scan evaluation (Figure 18), and cross-shape correspondence testing (A.2.7). These broaden annotation requirements, input domains and evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Table 3 replaces the PartSAM variant using Point-SAM's encoder with the complete Point-SAM model trained on the curated dataset, as explained in A.2.1. This changes the comparator within that experiment. The external comparator sets in the main interactive and automatic benchmarks remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experimental designs include training-data sweeps from 40k to 500k shapes, a training-from-scratch control, automatic prompt-budget sweeps from 256 to 1024 points, functional-map correspondence testing, and coarse/fine semantic-label evaluation. Table 3 also replaces an encoder-swap control with whole-model Point-SAM training. The original main benchmark protocols and stated training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends the existing encoder, data and connectivity analyses. It adds a pretrained-initialization ablation, direct data-scaling curves, prompt-density sensitivity, native-versus-lifted label comparisons, cross-shape consistency examples, and explicit failure analyses with randomly sampled galleries. These investigate scalability, initialization dependence, efficiency tradeoffs and failure conditions beyond v1's analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added scaling plot and result tables continue to report point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 4 and the retained Table 3 rows are unchanged. Table 3 replaces the encoder-swap results of 45.1 IoU@1 and 56.4 automatic IoU with 38.9 and 48.6 for retrained Point-SAM; these concern different comparators. New results include the scratch variant, scaling curves, prompt-budget tradeoffs, correspondence/failure examples and Table 6—for example, plane coarse/fine-average IoU of 53.5 for PartSAM versus 38.9 for PartField.

T1.justification: Equation (3)'s mathematical definition of total loss changes through the explicit IoU term and non-unit Dice coefficient. This is a limited formal-definition revision. The remaining mathematics is retained or elaborated through tensor-shape descriptions, without new theorems, proofs or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: native-3D promptable segmentation, a scalable dual-branch encoder, millions of curated shape-part pairs, and strong interactive and automatic performance. The added experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v1's limitations discussion focuses on the absence of semantic labels. v3 retains that limitation and adds explanations involving rare parts, engraved details, ambiguous part hierarchies and irregular generated or scanned geometry. It acknowledges SAMesh's fine surface-detail strengths and adds interpretations of initialization, scaling and correspondence results, substantially refining the account of applicability and failure.

D1.justification: Expanded A.1 documents voxel and channel dimensions, encoder processing, decoder token handling, the IoU head, previous-mask embeddings and additional curation safeguards. A.2.5 explains the existing graph-cut refinement in greater detail. These are mainly disclosures about retained components. v3 also replaces the promised future code/model release with a project-page pointer; the PDFs do not establish what resources are actually available there.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for functional maps, 3DCoMPAT++, object scans and OmniObject3D, and removes Dosovitskiy et al. when replacing the encoder-specific ablation description. The main related-work organization and novelty positioning against lifting, clustering and existing promptable methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Although the main narrative is largely retained, appendix exposition is substantially expanded and reorganized. The short implementation section becomes four subsections covering the pipeline, previous prompts, curation and training; the architecture-ablation discussion is rewritten into separate comparisons, and limitations become an extended failure discussion. There are also localized wording corrections, updated headers and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 9–11, 13–14 and 17–18, covering interior comparisons, labels, scaling, correspondences and failures. It expands Tables 3 and 5 and adds Table 6. Existing v1 Figures 9–11 are retained as v3 Figures 12, 15 and 16. These additions and revised displays substantially change visual presentation beyond pagination or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for scalability through direct data-size experiments and initialization controls, broadens evaluation, and makes previously narrow limitations concrete through failure cases. Expanded implementation explanations also improve reproducibility. Replacing the encoder-only Point-SAM ablation sacrifices one isolated control, while some new evaluation details and the relationship between the revised loss and unchanged main scores remain unclear. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidential support, transparency and assessment of applicability.
